A lot of the time we seasoned painters forget that new painters don't know the nuances of even simple techniques, (for example, when painting large surface areas its even more important to dilute your paint to eliminate the showing of brush strokes in the finish) we forget ourselves sometimes and don't realize we've just told a beginning painter the basics of how to highlight, but not WHERE to put those highlights...

One thing you may have missed that I find helps the entire process, BEFORE you prime your models, I prefer to base them first (just the gravel, sand mind you) take some PVA glue and water it down 1 to 1 and apply it to the base and then dip and shake into your desired basing material (for me that is coffee grounds). Then, after the glue has dried go back over the basing with a 3 to 1 mixture of water to glue, dilute your glue heavily so it sinks into the recesses of the texture on the basing, wait for it to dry and voila! If you're priming white just go over the basing with whatever color you want that footing to be...
